$comment: Persat Finance devnet cluster configuration.
Devnet is the target cluster for the MVP. The authoritative documents say
'testnet' throughout, which is correct as PRODUCT language — users read it
as 'not real money'. It should not be read as the Solana testnet cluster:
* Solana's own docs say 'Application developers should target Devnet'.
Testnet exists for validator operators stress-testing pre-release
validator software, and is documented as often unstable during upgrade
cycles.
* Decisively: the Pyth receiver program is deployed on mainnet and devnet,
but not on Solana testnet. On testnet the protocol would have no BTC/USD
price at all, and every price-dependent action would fail closed.
Every address below marked PLACEHOLDER must be replaced before deployment.
This file contains no secrets and never will: it holds public addresses
only. Keypairs live in a secret manager, never in this repository.
$rpcNote: The public endpoint is rate-limited (100 requests / 10s per IP) and is not
intended for production traffic. Provision a dedicated Helius, QuickNode,
or Triton endpoint before the indexer and keeper run continuously, and set
it via SOLANA_RPC_URL rather than editing this file.

programs.$comment: Deterministic placeholders derived from a domain string. Replace with real generated program keypairs at deployment time.

oracle.$comment: The feed id identifies the feed, not an account, and is identical on every cluster. Pyth is a pull oracle: a client posts a signed Hermes update into a PriceUpdateV2 account, then passes that account to the instruction that needs it. No pusher keypair exists.

$comment: Devnet has no canonical tBTC, zBTC, or USDC faucet. Standard practice is
to mint your own SPL tokens with matching decimals and treat them as
stand-ins, which is exactly what the /faucet route is for.
Collateral MUST be 8 decimals: the whitelist registry rejects any other
value for a collateral asset, because the risk parameters are calibrated
against real tBTC/zBTC precision.

collateral.$riskNote: tBTC is the more decentralised option but has thinner Solana liquidity, so a fast liquidation could face real slippage. Consider a stricter maxLtv than zBTC once real liquidity is measurable.
zBTC has a smaller validator set but deeper Solana liquidity, so liquidation executes closer to true market price.

loanCurrency.$comment: Treated as exactly $1. No oracle feed, by protocol policy.
Treated as exactly $1. No oracle feed, by protocol policy.

excluded.$comment: Excluded from collateral by explicit protocol policy, not oversight. add_asset_type is governance-gated so none of these can be added without a deliberate, visible governance action.
excluded.cbBTC: Single centralised company holds the backing reserves.

fees.$comment: 2% on both paths for the MVP. Separate fields so the paths can diverge later without a contract change. No configuration may exceed the 5% protocol cap.

governance.$comment: Three independent signer public keys. Publish public keys only; the keypairs belong in a secret manager. Standard actions are 2-of-3 with a 24h timelock; emergency pause is 1-of-3 with no timelock, and unpausing requires the full 2-of-3.

keeper.$comment: Funded for transaction fees only. It never custodies user funds and has no discretion over amounts: it chooses only when to ask, and every figure is recomputed on-chain from state and the verified oracle price.
